newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana says S.African raiders may be prosecuted.
newsitem.headline: Botswana says S.African raiders may be prosecuted.

text.p: Botswana said on Friday that soldiers from South Africa's apartheid era security forces who took part in cross border raids targeting African National Congress (ANC) activists could face prosecution in Gaborone.
Foreign Affairs Minister Mompati Merafhe denied reports that Botswana's policy was to forgive and forget, telling reporters:
"The decision whether or not to prosecute would be taken by the Attorney General, based on evidence at hand. The government would not intervene," Merafhe said.

He was reacting to reports in South African and Botswana newspapers quoting Botswana's High Commissioner to South Africa, Oteng Tebape, as saying he did not anticipate his government would call for the raiders' extradition.

Deputy Attorney General Abednico Tafa has said he favours prosecution and that any indemnity granted the alleged killers by the South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission would carry no weight in Botswana.
Other official sources in Gaborone said on Friday they should face justice in Botswana.
The truth commission headed by Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu has asked Botswana for permission to hold a hearing in the capital Gaborone.
Merafhe said a decision on the request had not yet been taken because questions posed to the truth commission by Botswana had not yet been answered.
"We are hamstrung until we get the answers," he added.

The truth commission wants to probe cross border raids by the old South African Defence Force into Botswana. A former Pretoria security policeman also confessed to the commission that he was part of a raid in which two children were killed.
